claim: SoL-Pi reduces recorded token traffic by 44.7–49.0% and API cost by about one third compared to Pi on EdgeBench.
quote: On the 51-task EdgeBench evaluation, SoL-Pi achieves performance comparable to Pi across GPT-5.6 Sol and Opus 5 while reducing recorded token traffic by 44.7–49.0% and API cost by about one third.

claim: SoL-Pi reduces API cost by 50.0% relative to Codex on GPT-5.6 Sol and by 54.3% relative to Claude Code on Opus 5.
quote: SoL-Pi reduces API cost by 50.0% relative to Codex on GPT-5.6 Sol and by 54.3% relative to Claude Code on Opus 5.

claim: The search yielded four specific mechanisms: Action Fusion, Online Context Compact, ObservationPack, and Evidence-Preserving Reducer.
quote: The search yields four reusable mechanisms that pass capability-constrained selection: Action Fusion, Online Context Compact, ObservationPack, and Evidence-Preserving Reducer.

claim: Action Fusion combines a mutation and its follow-up command into one request, reducing API calls from three to two.
quote: Action Fusion combines a mutation and its follow-up command into one request, reducing API calls from three to two.

claim: Online Context Compact applies compaction only when projected savings exceed the rewrite cost.
quote: Online Context Compact evaluates compaction at subtask completion and applies it only when projected savings exceed the rewrite cost.

claim: ObservationPack replaces large results with a stable handle and a 1 KB excerpt after the first two provider requests.
quote: ObservationPack sends large results in full for the first two provider requests, then replaces them with a stable handle and a 1 KB excerpt.

claim: Evidence-Preserving Reducer uses a low-cost model to compact results with deterministic verification and fallback to the original on failure.
quote: Evidence-Preserving Reducer uses a low-cost model to compact results, with deterministic verification and fallback to the original on failure.

claim: Held-out results never feed back into the search loop to prevent validation failures from being patched into task-specific solutions.
quote: Held-out results never feed back into the Auto-Research Loops: a failed validation rejects the candidate without triggering further optimization.

claim: The search set comprises 535 executable environments, including 495 repository tasks and 40 synthetic tasks.
quote: The search set comprises 535 executable environments: 495 repository tasks derived from GitHub issue–pull request pairs and 40 synthetic tasks with executable success verifiers.

claim: SoL-Pi [Efficiency] uses 1.10 B tokens, which is 49.0% fewer than Pi, while retaining 93.7% of Pi’s average score.
quote: The Efficiency point uses a total of 1.10 B tokens, 49.0% fewer than Pi, while retaining 93.7% of Pi’s average score (42.0 vs. 44.8).

claim: SoL-Pi developed with GPT-5.6 Sol retains 94.3% of Pi’s average score on Opus 5 without further search or adaptation.
quote: On Opus 5, it retains 94.3% of Pi’s average score while reducing token traffic by 44.7% and API cost by 33.5%, relative to Pi’s point estimates.

claim: SoL-Pi reduces total model cost by 26.3% compared to Pi on Terminal-Bench 4.
quote: Compared with Pi, SoL-Pi reduces total model cost by 26.3% ($211.12 vs. $286.45) and cost per solved task by 11.6% ($14.07 vs. $15.91).

claim: SoL-Pi achieves the lowest cost per passed problem on IMO 2026.
quote: SoL-Pi passes three of six problems at a total model cost of $62.69, achieving the lowest cost per passed problem ($20.90), compared with $22.89 for Codex and $25.32 for Pi.

claim: The SoL-Pi swarm reduces API cost by 26.8% relative to the Pi baseline swarm under the same execution budget.
quote: Under the same execution budget, the SoL-Pi swarm reduces API cost by 26.8% relative to the Pi baseline swarm, while the single agent remains least expensive.

claim: The complete SoL-Pi stack reduces token traffic by 44.7–49.0% on EdgeBench.
quote: On EdgeBench, the best-performing candidates improve model performance by 5.3–12.8% and token efficiency by 9.8–18.2%, while the complete stack reduces token traffic by 44.7–49.0% and token cost by about one third at comparable performance.

claim: Mechanism activation varies across backends, with lower trigger rates under Opus 5.
quote: Figure 6 shows that mechanism activation varies across backends. Trigger rate is the fraction of tasks on which a mechanism activates, while trigger intensity is the mean number of activations per triggered task. Both are lower under Opus 5, which may reflect the harness being optimized exclusively on GPT-5.6 Sol trajectories.

claim: ObservationPack becomes more selective in the full stack due to overlap with Evidence-Preserving Reducer.
quote: ObservationPack becomes more selective in the full stack, potentially due to overlap with Evidence-Preserving Reducer on observation-heavy trajectories.

claim: Shortening context can reduce prompt-cache reuse when it changes a previously cached prefix.
quote: Shortening context can reduce prompt-cache reuse when it changes a previously cached prefix [39].

claim: GPU-dependent Terminal-Bench 4 tasks were excluded due to infrastructure limits.
quote: Note. GPU-dependent Terminal-Bench 4 tasks were excluded due to infrastructure limits.

claim: Comparisons on each configuration’s own triggered-task subset do not isolate interaction effects.
quote: This pattern is consistent with complementarity in the evaluated stack, although comparisons on each configuration’s own triggered-task subset do not isolate interaction effects.

claim: Running complete auto-research loops is computationally expensive, making controlled comparisons challenging.
quote: Running complete auto-research loops in our environment is computationally expensive, making controlled comparisons of search breadth and depth under a fixed budget particularly challenging.

claim: The single agent and coordinators use GPT-5.6 Sol at xhigh, while all workers use GPT-5.6 Luna at xhigh.
quote: The single agent and coordinators use GPT-5.6 Sol at xhigh; all workers use GPT-5.6 Luna at xhigh.
